what_happened_next.text:
Apple grew to about five times its starting value, and Microsoft to almost four times. Nintendo nearly doubled, while the US share basket a little more than doubled. Bonds gained only a little. The five years included a pandemic and large changes in interest rates, none of which made prices move in a straight line.

The pandemic arrived during these five years. WHO described it as a pandemic in March 2020 and listed its first COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use that December. In 2022, the Fed began raising interest rates. That July, Webb’s first full set of scientific images offered striking new views of space.

These changes formed the setting for the returns, but there is no simple rule assigning each gain to one event. The companies and broad baskets experienced the same years differently. Nintendo’s strong gain did not match Apple’s, and cash followed another path entirely. A good result can still come second or third; coming first is not the only way an investment can grow.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: People watched interest rates, climate talks, new games and an approaching spacecraft flyby. Technology companies reported their results.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: A broad basket and individual companies had different outcomes. Even strong gains over five years included periods when prices fell.
reflection.what_faded_away: A holiday hit or one strong quarter could not settle the next five years. Good company news did not remove the risk of its shares.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The pandemic was unknown. It is easier to explain the eventual winners after seeing the chart than to choose them beforehand.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: Nintendo’s Switch and Animal Crossing: New Horizons became popular ways to play during the pandemic. In the year ended March 2021, Switch sales rose 37% and profit from running the business rose 82%. New hits kept the business going: Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom sold 19.5 million copies by September 2023, and the Mario movie brought in more money from Nintendo’s characters. Those successes supported the shares.

Apple’s devices and services produced a huge holiday quarter in 2020, with revenue reaching $111.4 billion. Growth later cooled: sales fell slightly in the quarter ended September 2023. Yet services set another sales record, and Apple spent nearly $25 billion paying cash to shareholders and buying back shares that quarter. The investment finished far ahead, even as sales growth slowed near the end.

Microsoft grew as businesses paid for Azure computing services and Office subscriptions. Its annual revenue reached $211.9 billion in the year ended June 2023. Even with weak personal-computer sales, Azure and other cloud revenue grew 26% in that final quarter. Its cloud business grew, and the company began adding new AI tools. The investment finished far ahead.
